To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the dual surfactant approach to shape control of CuNPs is a viable approach to the production of shape-specific CuNPS; 2) the surfactants adsorb onto the facets of the growing nanocrystal in a competitive fashion, and 3) the geometric CuNP shape is an important factor in the skin permeation and cellular internalisation of CuNPs.
the dual surfactant control of the nanoparticle shape is an interesting and novel approach to the synthesis of shape-specific copper nanoparticles with the potential for biomedical applications.
we have successfully synthesized five novel copper nanoparticles with unique morphologies, and that the shape of the nanoparticles has an effect on their ability to cross the epidermal skin barrier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the synthesis of shape-specific copper nanocrystals and its biomedical application as a drug delivery platform.
a new approach for synthesising shape-specific, dual-surfactant mediated, copper nanoparticles and the application thereof for skin permeation studies and drug delivery.
the synthesis of shape-specific copper nanocrystals and its application in drug-delivery systems for transdermal skin permeation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dual surfactant approach to control the shape of copper nanoparticles is an interesting method for the synthesis of novel nano-geometrical structures and its application as a drug delivery vehicle is promising for the treatment of skin diseases.
the dual surfactant control of the CuNP shape is a viable method for shape control in the biomedical field of skin permeation studies and drug delivery systems.
the dual surfactant approach to the synthesis of the CuNPS was successful in producing shape specific CuNPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape of the copper nanoparticles is determined by the surfactant adsorption on to the facets.
we successfully synthesised shape specific, copper nanocrystals with controlled surfactant adsorption and that the geometric CuNPS have potential in drug delivery.
a dual control of surfactants was successfully used to direct the synthesis of novel, geometric CuNPs with the potential to act as drug delivery systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dual surfactant-mediated adsorption of cetyl trimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS) onto the facets of the nanocrystals directs the shape organisation of copper nanocrystals.

the dual surfactant approach is an efficient method for shape design and that the shape of a nano-geometry is a significant factor in the transbarrier transport and internalisation of the nano-geometrical copper particles.
shape control can be achieved by competitive surfactant adsorption on different facets and the skin permeation of the NPs can be tailored for specific applications
